title: Meta: supplement and weight ads must target adults 18+
rule_summary: Ads for dietary or health supplements and weight loss or gain products must be targeted to people aged 18 or older. Copy that addresses or features teens is a red flag.
source_title: Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness (Transparency Center)
citation: Meta Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness
violating_examples: Back-to-school energy for students (supplement ad, all ages).
fix_patterns: Remove references to minors; remind the company to set 18+ targeting.

title: Meta: no claims to cure listed incurable diseases
rule_summary: Meta ads may not claim to cure, heal or eliminate diabetes, herpes, thyroid conditions, psoriasis, Ebola, cancer, autism, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS or HIV, even when the claim comes from health professionals. Meta's rule doesn't cover symptom-management claims, but FDA rules still do.
source_title: Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness (Transparency Center)
citation: Meta Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness

title: Meta: no appearance-shaming or clickbait health claims
rule_summary: Weight and cosmetic ads can't attack someone's appearance, body parts or hygiene, or show close-ups of pinched fat. Health ads can't use clickbait: sensational or extreme claims, or promises of specific outcomes within a set time without qualifiers.
source_title: Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness (Transparency Center)
citation: Meta Advertising Standards: Health and Wellness
fix_patterns: Remove the appearance attack or the timed promise.
